hints: Differentiate the implicit curve term by term, including 6y²(dy/dx) and 3x²(dy/dx)+6xy.
Collect derivative terms and isolate dy/dx to reach the displayed quotient.
walkthrough:
Differentiate both sides of $2y^3 - 3x^2 y - x^3 = 16$ implicitly with respect to $x$:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(2y^3\right) = 6y^2\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$$
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(-3x^2 y\right) = -3\left(2xy + x^2\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}\right) = -6xy - 3x^2\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$$
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(-x^3\right) = -3x^2, \quad \dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(16) = 0$$

Assemble the terms into one equation:
$$6y^2\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} - 6xy - 3x^2\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} - 3x^2 = 0$$

Group terms involving $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$ on the left-hand side and move the other terms to the right:
$$\left(6y^2 - 3x^2\right)\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = 3x^2 + 6xy$$

ai_rubric.Implicit Differentiation: Identifies $6y^2\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ as the derivative of $2y^3$; Identifies $3x^2\dfrac{dy}{dx}+6xy$ as the derivative of $3x^2y$; Concludes with $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{x^2+2xy}{2y^2-x^2}$.

hints: A normal parallel to the y-axis means a horizontal tangent, so set the numerator x²+2xy to zero.
Treat x=0 and x=−2y separately, substitute each into the original curve, and retain every resulting point.
walkthrough:
Establish the condition for the normal to be parallel to the $y$-axis:
$$\text{If the normal is parallel to the } y\text{-axis (vertical), the tangent is horizontal: } \dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = 0$$
$$\dfrac{x^2 + 2xy}{2y^2 - x^2} = 0 \implies x^2 + 2xy = 0 \quad (\text{provided } 2y^2 - x^2 \neq 0)$$
$$x(x + 2y) = 0 \implies x = 0 \quad \text{or} \quad x = -2y$$

Case 1: Substitute $x = 0$ into the original curve equation $2y^3 - 3x^2 y - x^3 = 16$:
$$2y^3 - 3(0)^2 y - 0^3 = 16$$
$$2y^3 = 16 \implies y^3 = 8 \implies y = 2$$
$$\text{Check denominator: } 2(2^2) - 0^2 = 8 \neq 0 \implies (0, 2) \text{ is a valid point.}$$

Case 2: Substitute $x = -2y$ into the original curve equation $2y^3 - 3x^2 y - x^3 = 16$:
$$2y^3 - 3(-2y)^2 y - (-2y)^3 = 16$$
$$2y^3 - 3\left(4y^2\right)y - \left(-8y^3\right) = 16$$
$$2y^3 - 12y^3 + 8y^3 = 16$$
$$-2y^3 = 16 \implies y^3 = -8 \implies y = -2$$
$$x = -2(-2) = 4$$
$$\text{Check denominator: } 2(-2)^2 - 4^2 = 2(4) - 16 = 8 - 16 = -8 \neq 0 \implies (4, -2) \text{ is a valid point.}$$

State the coordinates of the points:
$$(0, 2) \quad \text{and} \quad (4, -2)$$

ai_rubric.Finding Stationary Points: Equates the derivative to zero and solves for $x$, or for $x$ in terms of $y$. Derives $(4,-2)$. The final result is $(0,2)$ and $(4,-2)$.
